notes.title: Some video games that are like Bandersnatch, but better
notes.notes:
If you ve choosed-and-adventured through Bandersnatch, the recent Black Mirror thing on Netflix, and aren t already a fan of experimental interactive fiction: I envy you. It means you re able to play actually good examples of interactive fiction for the first time.

Sure, Bandersnatch has funny lines, surprises and scene stealing performances from Will Poulter doing a pretty much exactly how I, the writer, talk in real life voice. But as a whole, video games have been iterating deeper on the main themes of control, authenticity, forced choice, meta-recursion and non-linearity for years, without also including an unhelpful portrayal of paranoid schizophrenia. When you love enough people who hear voices and suffer from castigatory delusions, maybe you become less enthused about media which depicts sufferers committing murders or throwing themselves off buildings. Fix it, Brooker. The same plotpoint was in White Christmas and it was shit back then.

(more…)

notes.title: Magic Circle devs announce co-op horror Blackout Club
notes.notes: The immersive sim supergroup at Question, the studio behind The Magic Circle, have announced their next game. The Blackout Club is a cooperative multiplayer game starring teens who discover a secret nighttime society of sleepwalking adults meeting in tunnels beneath their small town, then set about spying on them, recording evidence, and trying to find their missing friend. notes.title: Update With Some Bugfixes
notes.notes:
Today we are updating with an important (if very rare) bugfix. There was an issue where *spoilers ahead* [spoiler]damage done by the parasite ability did not properly send life back into the crack system[/spoiler]. This [i]could[/i] be made into a spiral of fail (by a truly dedicated player) that might create an impossible to recover from resource situation.  We have a fix, as well as an attempt to correct the problem in save files of affected players.

Special thanks to Jetz on the forums, who spent a lot of time isolating the problem and sent us incredibly useful save files and repro steps. The bug was rare enough that no one else has ever reported it, but Jetz pushed the system as far as it would go and uncovered the issue.

As always, we are super grateful to our awesome players. Thanks for checking out the game and hope you have enjoyed it!

-Question

notes.title: Ides of March Update, IGF Nomination, and SXSW!
notes.notes:
This update has a bunch of miscellaneous tweaks and fixes to various systems as well as some usability improvements. Some of the highlights include improvements in the way music is delivered, D-Pad support in all parts of mindspace (for our gamepad players), some AI improvements, and some unobtrusive control reminders if we detect you have been away from the game for a while. The full list can be seen in the Tech Support forum.

In addition, [i]The Magic Circle[/i] is up for an Excellence in Narrative award at this year's IGF! If you are at GDC come say hi to rujuro and Nullspeak in the IGF area, if not you can still watch the awards live on twitch the evening of March 16th.

[b]And there's still more![/b] KainAsylum will be showing the game at SXSW in Austin, TX where we are up for the Gamer's Voice Award.  If you are going to be there stop by, say hi, and maybe vote for us if it's the kind of thing you'd like to do.

Thanks again to everyone who has played the game, we are extremely grateful for your support.

-Question

notes.notes:

There are also a number of small geometry and texture tweaks, as well as some fixes to how the player behaves in certain collision situations. Please let us know if you see anything bizarre! As always the full change list can be seen in the Tech Support Forum.

Thanks again to all the players who have given [i]The Magic Circle[/i] a chance, we appreciate it and hope you enjoyed the game!

-Question

notes.title: Wot I Think: The Magic Circle
notes.notes:
The Magic Circle [Steam page] is a game about an unfinished game. A first person puzzle/exploration/action game about a fictional game also called The Magic Circle, to be precise. After years of development hell, The Magic Circle’s fans look upon it with a mixture of breathless anticipation and derision. Those few staff who still work on it either desperately want out or refuse to abandon their impossible dreams. Now you are inside this half-made game, exploring what it is and what it was, how it ran aground, whether it belongs to its creators or its players, and perhaps either redeeming it or destroying it.

It’s out now. The real Magic Circle that is, not the fictional one. Here’s what I think.

… [visit site to read more]

In the meantime, enjoy some pre-release fun over at [url=www.magiccirclegame.com]magiccirclegame.com[/url]

Question

notes.title: Oops, We Goofed! The Game is Still Available
notes.notes:
As we mentioned, we intended to take the game off of the store to prepare for the full release in the next couple weeks.  What we did not know is that Valve does not give developers the power to control availability themselves.

We have reached out where we can to find out how we go about removing the game from the store, so it could disappear at any time.  Until then, you can still get the Deluxe Edition at the reduced Early Access price.  

Sorry for the confusion, there are clearly things we are still learning about Steam.


Thanks for your understanding,
Question/TMC Team

notes.title: Some VO / Story edits coming...
notes.notes:
Hey Early Access folks. 

Because many of you have played through the game in its current form and you're all paying customers, we wanted to be as transparent as possible with you (Ish Gilder would be mortified). 

Long story shorter - as some of you know already, TMC is very talk-heavy in act 3, for the amount of game that's there. Before we recorded some of the bigger scenes, we had some ideas about how to improve the gameplay-to-chatter ratio there. But when we finally evaluated those ideas seriously as a team, we realized they had their own potential to feel like padding, and that seemed bad - so we walked away and got busy with other critical issues. That left you guys needing to be more patient with the story near the end than we're comfortable with.

As a result, we're going to make some edits to make the script on the critical path a little leaner. Some of you may not even notice; we don't want to make it out to be world-shaking. But if you're a huge fan of act 3 exactly as it is, well, we salute your superhuman patience, and now would be the time to video-capture the "rough cut", as it were. We will try to make that content available either in game or out, somewhere, if you're into the game equivalent of deleted scenes.

Thank you for playing, and for helping us to make TMC better.

- Question (Jordan, Stephen, Kain, and Pat)

notes.title: Premature Evaluation: The Magic Circle
notes.notes:
Each week Marsh Davies plays unfinished and broken games on Early Access and usually tries to come up with an introductory sentence which says exactly this while using imagery appropriate to the idiom of the given week s game. But the idiom of this week s game is being an unfinished and broken game! So, job done. It s The Magic Circle [Steam page], a game set within a game, in which the player edits the properties of the world around him while exploring the strata of the game s many abandoned developmental stages, unravelling the story of its creators in the process.

I have tamed Jim Rossignol s bumhole. I ve also made Jim Rossignol s bumhole fireproof, which is just as well, since Jim Rossignol s bumhole spews gouts of flame when angered. Jim Rossignol s bumhole has a lightning rod jammed in it, too, which deactivates forcefields. With my latest effort, Jim Rossignol s bumhole has sprouted a little propeller, allowing Jim Rossignol s bumhole to fly about. John Walker s angry red Weeto has many of the same properties, and it should surprise no one that Alec Meer s huge husky third leg is shaped like a ginormous mushroom.

… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Development Hell: The Magic Circle On Steam Early Access
notes.notes:
You can now buy and play Ion Storm and BioShock alumnus Jordan Thomas’s emergent oddity The Magic Circle [The Magic Circle], but do be aware that it’s not finished yet. No, I know that’s the point of the game – that you roam around an unfinished vapourware game, rewriting it from the inside – but I mean it’s really not finished.

The Magic Circle arrived on Steam Early Access today. In all the layers of metafiction, it may be the most The Magic Circle-y version of The Magic Circle you’ll get.
